projects.name: allacampingplatser
projects.description: A comprehensive camping site discovery platform for Sweden that allows users to search, filter, and explore camping locations across the country. The application features an interactive map with location markers and clusters, detailed information pages for each camping site, and a responsive design that works seamlessly on both mobile and desktop devices. The platform integrates with Contentful CMS for dynamic content management and uses Mapbox for advanced mapping capabilities.
projects.shortDescription: An interactive map-based platform for discovering and exploring camping sites across Sweden with advanced filtering and search capabilities.
features: Interactive Map with Location Markers and Clusters
Responsive Design for Mobile and Desktop
Location Detail Pages with Rich Content
Hover Highlighting Between List and Map Views
Custom Animation Effects for UI Elements

caseStudy.problem: Camping information in Sweden is scattered across municipal websites, PDFs and forums — there was no single place to browse every campsite on a map, compare them and plan a trip. I wanted a product that solved a real discovery problem end to end, and that forced me to handle real-world constraints: geodata at scale, content operations, SEO and performance on mobile networks.
caseStudy.approach: I built it as a content-driven Next.js application. Every campsite lives in Contentful with a structured content model (location, facilities, imagery, seasonal info), which keeps the data editable without deployments. The frontend statically generates a page per campsite for SEO, while the map experience is fully client-side and interactive. The stack is deliberately boring where it should be — TypeScript, Next.js, Tailwind — so the effort could go into the parts users feel: the map, the filtering and the speed.

craft.title: Map performance at scale
craft.text: Rendering hundreds of markers kills the frame rate on mobile, so markers are clustered and the map only renders what the viewport needs. Panning and zooming stay smooth even on mid-range phones.

craft.title: List ↔ map as one surface
craft.text: Hovering a campsite in the list highlights its marker on the map and vice versa, so the two views behave as one connected surface instead of two parallel UIs.

craft.title: SEO as architecture, not afterthought
craft.text: Each campsite gets a statically generated, indexable page with structured content from the CMS — the map is the experience, but the pages are what search engines and shared links land on.

craft.title: Two languages, one content model
craft.text: Swedish and English are handled through the CMS localization model rather than duplicated content, keeping translations in sync with a single source of truth.

caseStudy.outcome: The platform is live at allacampingplatser.se and in active use. [FYLL I: 2–3 verifierbara utfall — t.ex. antal campingplatser i databasen, organisk trafik/månad, antal indexerade sidor i Google Search Console, Lighthouse-poäng]
